assessments.reasoning: After a successful lookup finds no own descriptor, OrdinaryGet retrieves the prototype. A null prototype ends the lookup with undefined. An object prototype receives the original property key and Receiver through its own [[Get]], whose completion passes back to the caller.

challenge.method: Trace an own data property valued undefined, then an absent property with an exotic prototype and a distinct Receiver.
challenge.results: The own descriptor bypasses prototype lookup even though its value is undefined. In the absent case the prototype's internal method receives both original arguments and can throw. Delegation requires no assumption that the prototype uses OrdinaryGet.

limitations: An existing own descriptor follows the later data or accessor branch.
Delegated `[[Get]]` can complete normally or throw. The claim addresses the missing-descriptor branch of OrdinaryGet.
Node.js v24.4.1 provides a behavioral control. The normative finding rests on the pinned 15th-edition specification.
